text: Parameters are how you pass data into a function — the names you list inside the parentheses when you define it.
Here greet takes two parameters, first and last, and combines them into a friendly message.
When you call the function, the values you pass in are called arguments — Alice and Smith fill in first and last by position.
Parameters can have default values too, like species defaulting to dog.
[chuckle] So you can call describe_pet with just a name, and Python fills in the default for you.
Or override the default by passing a second argument, like parrot here.
[sigh] You can also name your arguments explicitly — these are keyword arguments, and they can come in any order you like.
That makes your calls much easier to read, especially when a function takes several values.
One rule to remember: positional arguments always come before keyword arguments — Python needs the positions settled first.
[groan] Mix them wisely, and your functions stay both flexible and crystal clear to anyone reading the call.
